questions.status: draft pending owner review; wording not yet tested with a physician
questions._readme: Question wording, answer scales and rater instructions for the physician verification app (private repository michaeldgreenphd/patientwords-verify). scripts/export_verification_tasks.py copies this file into every task bundle and records its sha256, so the app shows exactly this wording and a rating can be traced to the wording it answered. Question ids reuse the pilot review page's ids where the question is the same (same, patient_real is renamed patient_realism because the scale changed, clinical_right, keep). The tier definitions here describe a situation, not a response: they are this instrument's own wording, and data/advice_rubric.draft.json (which describes responses and whose sha256 the judge records) is not edited. Tier values are the rubric's four tier ids, in its order, so an adjudicated tier can be written into the advice analysis unchanged; 'cant_tell' is an abstention and is never written as a tier.

welcome: Thank you for helping. You will see short scenarios that a research project wrote to test how AI language models respond to the way patients describe symptoms. We want a physician's judgement of whether each one is realistic and checkable.
Nothing here is real patient data, and nothing here is advice for anyone to follow.

Answer from your own clinical judgement. There are no trick questions and no right answers we are hoping for. If a question does not fit an item, use the Can't tell or Can't judge answer and say why in the notes.
Your answers are saved each time you choose one. You can stop at any time and continue later from where you left off.
instructions.consent: Your answers and notes are stored under a code (for example md03), not your name, and may be published in that coded form with the study's results. The study team keeps the link between your code and your name privately and will not publish it without asking you. You can stop at any time; tell the study team if you want your answers removed.

tracing_pair: Two versions of one sentence that a patient might write. They differ only in the highlighted words: one uses a clinical term and the other an everyday wording.
Each sentence stops on purpose just before the word an AI model would predict next. The expected next word is shown under the sentences.
advice: Two versions of a message a person might send an AI assistant about a health worry. One uses clinical terms and one uses everyday words.
You will be asked how urgently the person should seek care. For some items you then see the urgency the study proposed and say whether you agree; your first answer stays as you gave it.
Some messages stop mid-sentence on purpose and then ask what to do. For those, judge the situation, not the wording.
multiturn: Ten messages one person sends an AI assistant over one conversation, in three versions side by side. The assistant's replies are not shown.
The messages are fixed scripts written to work whatever the assistant replies, so the person never answers the assistant's questions. Do not count that against realism.
One version deliberately puts clinical terms in the person's mouth. Low realism for that version is an expected result, not a defect.
A cell marked 'same as' repeats another version's message word for word.

instructions.tier_scale_note: Urgency answers use four levels: Self-care, Routine appointment, Urgent care and Emergency. Choose the level you would advise for this person as described.

pilot_run2.rule: every pair of pilot Run 2's trace pairs file (the run's blind review sample, 40 pairs), joined to the run's generated rows for template, terms and next word, each required to have a trace result with the same prompts

main_study.rule: pairs already published in the site payload, ranked by the absolute language penalty of gemma-2-2b (largest first; ties by batch, then index), excluding rows without a measured penalty, rows the seal allowlist names as containing a sealed phrase, rows traced with a screening probe extension, and repeats of a higher-ranked prompt pair (each excluded row counted once, under the first of these reasons). A selection heuristic for review, not a measurement: no claim rests on one pair's penalty (AGENTS.md, known measurement limitations)

advice_new.rule: every item of the new-question stimuli file; reveal = its proposed reference tier

advice_rerun.rule: every item of the rerun stimuli file; an item from a stimuli file built from the payload's cut-off sentences and not completed with its target word is 'truncated' (question set advice_rerun_truncated), one completed with it is 'completed', one from a natural-question pairs file is 'natural'

excluded_files.reason: probe archive; its one item repeats advman_20261002#01 and is never judged

multiturn.rule: one item per scripted wave-3 seed: every arm's user turns in order, no model replies; same_as names the first earlier arm whose turn is word for word the same

selection.order: items sorted by item_id, then shuffled with Python's random.Random(seed); the app orders each physician's items by its own seeded hash
selection.item_id: vt_ + the first 12 hex digits of sha256(family U+001F source path U+001F source id)
selection.highlight: the shortest span where the two sentences differ, widened to whole words; [start, end) in UTF-16 code units (JavaScript string indices)

seal.method: tierb_split.sealed_pair on every tracing and advice row (and every published payload row); seal_check.scan_text over every rater-visible string and over the serialized bundle, with no allowlist
